intro: Hidden-neuron indices are arbitrary. Reordering a hidden layer preserves the represented function when its incoming and outgoing connections move together.
task: Apply a hidden-neuron permutation to both sides of a two-layer network.
requirements: input_weights has shape input-by-hidden, hidden_bias has length hidden, and output_weights has shape hidden-by-output. order is a permutation of 0..hidden-1.

Return {"input_weights": input_weights[:,order], "hidden_bias": hidden_bias[order], "output_weights": output_weights[order,:]}. New hidden position j corresponds to old position order[j]. This preserves elementwise-activation networks.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Swap hidden neurons
examples.output:
{'input_weights': [[2.0, 1.0], [4.0, 3.0]],
 'hidden_bias': [6.0, 5.0],
 'output_weights': [[8.0], [7.0]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Identity order
examples.output:
{'input_weights': [[1.0, 2.0]],
 'hidden_bias': [3.0, 4.0],
 'output_weights': [[5.0], [6.0]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Three-neuron cycle
examples.output:
{'input_weights': [[3.0, 1.0, 2.0]],
 'hidden_bias': [6.0, 4.0, 5.0],
 'output_weights': [[9.0], [7.0], [8.0]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Incoming connections are columns; outgoing connections are rows.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: The same order is needed on both sides, rather than the inverse on one side.

explanation: This parameter symmetry creates multiple parameter arrays for the same network function. Equality of predictions therefore does not imply equality of individual hidden-neuron weights.
The argument relies on applying the same elementwise nonlinearity to every hidden coordinate. A coordinate-specific operation would need its own parameters permuted as well.
